t.1.103.1: This renowned family of ours, fully endowed with virtues, has held sovereignty upon the earth, surpassing all other rulers of the earth.
t.1.103.2: Guarded by former kings who knew dharma and were great-souled, this lineage of ours has never at any time here come to ruin.
t.1.103.3: By me, by Satyavatī, and by the great-souled Kṛṣṇa it has been established once more in you, who are the threads that carry on the family line.
t.1.103.5: It is heard that there is a Yādava maiden suited to our lineage, and likewise the daughter of Subala, and also that of the lord of the Madras.
t.1.103.4: O son, so that this family may grow like the ocean, it must be arranged accordingly by me, and by you especially.
t.1.103.7: I think that they should be chosen for the continuation of this lineage, O best of the wise; or what do you think, O Vidura?
t.1.103.8: Vidura said: You are our father, you are our mother, you are our supreme guru. Therefore, having reflected yourself, do what is beneficial for this family.
t.1.103.6: They are of noble lineage, beautiful, and well protected in every way, and fit for a marriage alliance with you and with us; those bulls among kṣatriyas are worthy kin.
t.1.103.9: Then he heard from the brahmins about Gāndhārī, the daughter of Subala: having worshipped Hara, the boon-granting god who destroyed the eyes of Bhaga, the auspicious Gāndhārī, it is said, had obtained a boon of a hundred sons.
t.1.103.11: Subala hesitated there, thinking, "He is blind." But having carefully weighed with his mind the family, its renown and its conduct, he gave Gāndhārī, who walked in dharma, to Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
t.1.103.10: Having heard this as the truth, O Bhārata, Bhīṣma, the grandfather of the Kurus, then sent word to the king of Gāndhāra.
t.1.103.12: Gāndhārī, too, heard that Dhṛtarāṣṭra was blind, and that her father and mother intended to give her to him, O Bhārata.
t.1.103.13: Then the lovely lady, wholly devoted to her vow of fidelity to her husband, took a cloth, folded it many times over, and bound it upon her own eyes, O king, having firmly resolved, “I shall not surpass my husband.”
t.1.103.14: Then Śakuni, son of the king of Gāndhāra, came to the Kauravas, bringing his sister, who was endowed with supreme beauty and splendor.
t.1.103.15: Having given his sister along with a fitting retinue, the hero, honored in return by Bhīṣma, went back again to his own city.
t.1.103.16: Gāndhārī too, the fair-hipped one, by her virtue, her conduct and her deeds, brought contentment to all the Kurus, O Bhārata.
t.1.103.17: Having won the favour of them all by her conduct, she, wholly devoted to her vow of fidelity to her husband, would not even in speech make mention of other men, however virtuous their vows.
